A small vocabulary for big ideas

Token
A piece of text represented by an integer ID. Here, one Unicode character.
Parameter / weight
A stored number adjusted during training. The model's learned behavior is encoded in these numbers.
Vector / dimension
A vector is an ordered list of numbers. Its dimension is the number of entries, not a physical direction. Our model uses 16, 24, or 32 entries per token.
Matrix / tensor
A matrix is a rectangular grid of numbers. A tensor generalizes this to any number of axes. Shapes tell you how many entries lie along each axis.
Activation
An intermediate number computed during a forward pass. Activations depend on the input; weights remain fixed until a training update.
Gradient
The local rate at which loss changes when a parameter changes. Backpropagation computes these rates throughout the model.
Batch / step / epoch
A batch is a set of training examples used for one update. This app averages four windows per optimizer step. An epoch usually means one pass over a training dataset; we count steps because windows are sampled with replacement.
Logit / softmax / loss
A logit is an unnormalized score. Softmax converts a set of scores into probabilities. Loss is a number measuring how poorly the prediction matched the target.
Attention head
One learned query/key/value subspace. Multiple heads make separate mixtures, then combine their outputs.
Inference / generation
Using learned weights to compute a prediction. Generation repeats inference while appending sampled tokens, without updating weights.
T · d · H · V
T = number of context positions; d = vector width; H = number of heads; V = vocabulary size. The attention formula also uses V for the value matrix; the surrounding context distinguishes it.
